text:
Aisha Khan: Heads-up, Evergreen Capital asked for an RFI row that explains 'controlled exit' from hosted fallback mid-POC — they want steps, audit trail, and a one-line procurement-safe clause. Can we draft and attach?

Leo Martin: We should call it 'Fallback Exit & Audit' in the capability matrix. Short bullets: 1) operator triggers exit via console or API, 2) active sessions finish on fallback target, 3) new requests routed to Dedicated, 4) full KV cache warm-up optionally requested. Include expected re-warm latency estimate.

Riley Chen: For numbers: re-warm to steady state ~15-30s for small seq len, up to ~2m for long-context sessions depending on cache priming. Add conservative estimate to RFI: worst-case 3 minutes.

Nora Gupta: Procurement insisted on a single-line 'safe' statement they can paste into their purchase order. Suggest: "Redwood will execute controlled fallback disable upon customer authorization; ongoing requests on fallback endpoints will complete subject to configured drain timeout (default 300s)." Thoughts?

Aisha Khan: Good. Legal wants a short liability pointer: fallback disabled by default; enabling fallback requires addendum with region and key controls. Legal-bot, can you provide suggested phrasing?

legal-bot: Suggested clause: "Controlled fallback is an optional operational mode that the Customer may enable via a signed addendum. Redwood disclaims liability for cross-region data egress when the customer has enabled fallback in writing; fallback may be disabled at any time by the Customer and will be subject to the configured drain timeout."

Leo Martin: Add a matrix column 'Exit behavior' with values: 'Immediate reject' (if customer forbids fallback), 'Graceful drain (default 300s)', 'Cache-warm + controlled cutover (opt-in)'.

CostBot: Baseline POC estimate (Dedicated, 2x mid-GPU): $14,500/mo. Controlled fallback enabled with 20% overflow shift to hosted adds: ~$2,900/mo. Emergency cross-region bursts if used heavily could add another $1.5k/mo. Assumptions: average session 180 tokens.

Riley Chen: Also include an appendix snippet showing the API call to disable fallback so SRE/procurement can see it in RFP appendix. Short curl example below.

Riley Chen: ```bash
# disable fallback for project 'evergreen-poc'
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/evergreen-poc/fallback:disable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode":"disable","drain_seconds":300}'
```

Aisha Khan: Perfect, put that in the technical appendix and link to the GKMS note about key rotation.

Nora Gupta: Security asked for evidence we store audit events for fallback actions. Can we say: "Audit logs (fallback enable/disable, who, when, reason) are retained per account for 540 days and are exportable to customer SIEM via syslog/forwarding"?

legal-bot: Confirmed acceptable. Add: "Exportable audit trail subject to customer subscription tier."

Leo Martin: I'm adding a small cell in the capability matrix: "Audit retention: 540d (exportable)" and "Drain timeout: default 300s (configurable)".

Aisha Khan: Any blockers on including a redacted SOC2 snippet? Sales said it helps procurement. Riley, can you attach the redacted page to the RFI bundle?

Riley Chen: Uploaded redacted SOC2 excerpt to the RFP folder: https://files.redwood.internal/sales/evergreen/soc2_excerpt_redacted.pdf :paperclip:

Nora Gupta: One more ask: procurement wants 'worst-case monthly delta' in a single cell. CostBot, can you compute worst-case if 50% of traffic bursts to hosted for 3 days?

CostBot: Worst-case estimate: baseline $14,500/mo. 50% overflow for 72 hours adds approx $9,000 (higher unit costs + egress). Worst-case monthly delta ~ +62% (~$23.5k total). Provide this as 'Worst-case monthly delta (3d, 50% overflow): +$9k (+62%)'.

Aisha Khan: Great. I'll fold the rows into the capability matrix: columns -> Feature, Default Behavior, Exit behavior, Audit retention, Cost delta (typical), Cost delta (worst-case). Then ping legal for sign-off language.

legal-bot: Suggest adding: "Fallback will remain disabled until the customer executes the Controlled Fallback Addendum, which specifies authorized users and regions. Activation without signed addendum is not permitted for accounts with data residency flags."

Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone — target send to Evergreen procurement by EOD. I'll attach the SOC2 page, API example, legal clause, and the cost cells. :white_check_mark:

Riley Chen: FYI we scheduled a short POC planning call with Evergreen on Tue 10:00 PT. Invite sent.

Aisha Khan: Awesome — on it.

Leo Martin: Adding a tiny note in the RFI appendix: 'If customer needs zero egress during fallback, set policy = reject and choose cache-warm cutover to Dedicated.'

Aisha Khan: Done. Closing thread after upload. :rocket:
